Lying, breaking promises, betraying trust and abusive disputing are signs of a hypocrite, even one who fasts, prays and claims to be Muslim; having one is a trait of hypocrisy.
When hypocrites mocked a labourer's half sa' gift as unneeded and a larger gift as showing off, a verse was revealed about those who scoff at voluntary givers.
Revelation confirms Zaid b. Arqam against Abdullah b. Ubayy, whom at death the Prophet shrouds in his shirt and prays over despite Umar, before a verse forbids it.
When some turned back on the way to Uhud, the Companions split over killing them, and the verse asking why they were two parties over the hypocrites came down.
Hudhaifa relates that twelve hypocrites of the Prophet's Ummah will be kept from Paradise, and says twelve of the people of Aqaba were enemies of Allah and His Messenger.
A gale blew at a hypocrite's death, two hypocrites face a fiercer fever on Resurrection Day, and a hypocrite is like a sheep straying between two flocks.
